description:
The five-minute example. Baseline and candidate are the same validity-controlled experiment, and the candidate uses an explicit generation-level ignored-reset-velocity fixture. Evidence metadata records that perturbation as ground truth for auditability; the verdict logic does not consume the label. The commanded action stream and selected validity declarations remain identical, while trajectory oracles establish and localize the numerical consequence.
Runs on CPU in under a second and needs no Isaac Lab and no GPU.
name: synthetic-reset-velocity-defect

tolerance.rationale: The quaternion is constructed analytically in float64. The 1e-9 guard is about 4.5 million float64 ULP at unit magnitude, so it is deliberately conservative; a breach indicates materially non-unit synthetic output.

Two milliradians is the predeclared illustrative pointwise engineering budget for this synthetic fixture. It is not derived from the 1.2 rad termination event: nominal and reset-fixture trajectories do not reach that threshold, so the event and decision oracles are negative controls rather than active gates in this case.
tolerance.scope: per-step absolute angle error, reduced over environments

tolerance.rationale: The same budget as the joint angle, because for a rotation built from a single joint angle the geodesic angle between two orientations equals the difference in that joint angle. Setting it any looser would make the orientation oracle quietly weaker than the joint-space one that it is supposed to corroborate.
tolerance.scope: per-step geodesic angle between orientations, reduced over environments

tolerance.rationale: One control step is the finest resolution the workload has. A one-step timing difference is observable but explicitly permitted; two or more fails the event contract. Neither subject crosses the threshold in the nominal fixture.
tolerance.scope: absolute difference in the first step at which |angle| exceeds 1.2 rad

tolerance.rationale: This is the decision a user actually consumes from this workload, so any disagreement at all is operationally meaningful. With 24 paired environments the finest resolvable rate below 1.0 would be 0.958, so a weaker threshold would be a statement about the sample size rather than about the workload.
tolerance.scope: fraction of environments whose survive/terminate outcome agrees

tolerance.rationale: The equivalence margin is set at the amplitude below which the time-averaged pole angle does not change the workload's termination statistics. It is intentionally wider than the per-step budget because a time average absorbs transient disagreement that the per-step oracle is there to catch.
tolerance.scope: mean over the horizon of |angle| per environment, paired across subjects
